title: Group Schemes of Finite Type over a Field

items.title: Group schemes of finite type over a field
items.statement: A group scheme of finite type over a field k is a finite-type k-scheme G with multiplication, identity, and inverse morphisms satisfying the group-object axioms. The definition includes nonreduced schemes. The group law is the functorial group law on G(R) for every k-algebra R.

references.title: J. S. Milne, Algebraic Groups (corrected 2022 printing)
references.locator: Chapter1 Definition1.1–1.3 and sections1.4–1.5, printed pp.6–8 (PDF17–19); complete definitions and all-algebra point criterion read.

items.strategy: Define all three structure morphisms and the scheme identities; evaluate them on arbitrary test schemes and algebras. No reducedness or smoothness is imposed.

items.title: Morphisms and closed subgroup schemes of group schemes
items.statement: A morphism of k-group schemes preserves multiplication, identity, and inverse. A closed subgroup scheme is a closed immersion that is a group-scheme morphism, with its induced group law.

references.title: J. S. Milne, Algebraic Groups (corrected 2022 printing)
references.locator: Chapter1 Definition1.1–1.3 and sections1.4–1.5, printed pp.6–8 (PDF17–19); complete definitions and all-algebra point criterion read.

items.strategy: Define preservation of each structure morphism and the closed subgroup with its induced group law; distinguish a closed subscheme from its rational points.

items.title: Closed subgroup schemes are detected on all algebra-valued points
items.statement: For a closed subscheme H of a k-group scheme G, H is a closed subgroup scheme if and only if H(R) is a subgroup of G(R) for every commutative k-algebra R.

references.title: J. S. Milne, Algebraic Groups (corrected 2022 printing)
references.locator: Chapter1 Definition1.1–1.3 and sections1.4–1.5, printed pp.6–8 (PDF17–19); complete definitions and all-algebra point criterion read.

items.strategy: Use the universal points of affine open charts of H times H and H to factor multiplication and inverse. The identity is tested over k. Uniqueness through the closed immersion glues these factors and transfers the group identities.

title: Group Schemes of Finite Type over a Field — Examples

items.title: The group schemes Ga, Gm, and GLn
items.statement: Verify the group-object formulas for the additive group Ga, multiplicative group Gm, and general linear group GLn.

references.title: J. S. Milne, Algebraic Groups (corrected 2022 printing)
references.locator: Chapter2 sections2.1–2.5/2.8, printed pp.39–41, and2.14 printedp.44 (PDF50–52/55); explicit affine formulas and alpha_p/mu_p scheme comparison read.

references.title: The Stacks Project, complete Groupoid Schemes chapter
references.locator: §5 Examples5.1–5.4, tags022U/040M/022V/022W, printed pp.5–6; all coordinate formulas and scheme-valued point descriptions read.

items.strategy: Write affine structure-ring maps for Ga and Gm and matrix multiplication/adjugate inversion on the determinant-open GLn. Check every group identity on arbitrary algebras and recover morphism identities by universal affine points.

items.title: Rational points do not detect the group-scheme structure of alpha_p and mu_p
items.statement: Over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic p>0, alpha_p(k) and mu_p(k) are singleton groups, while alpha_p and mu_p have different group-scheme laws and are not isomorphic as k-group schemes. Their underlying k-schemes are isomorphic.

items.strategy: Construct both finite closed group schemes on all algebras, translate the coordinate to identify their underlying schemes, and prove every group-like unit in k[x]/x^p with additive comultiplication is 1 by coefficient recurrence and the coefficient x^(p-1)y. This excludes an isomorphism to mu_p.
